column1: # cpe-extra.csv — component identity that Buildroot's own metadata does not give us.
# Read by scripts/compliance/cve-check.py. Three kinds of row:
#   1. CPE declared      — a cpe:2.3 string for a component Buildroot has no CPE_ID for,
#                          so it gets checked instead of counted as an unchecked gap.
#   2. CPE=NONE          — the component genuinely has no NVD presence. NOTES must say
#                          why, and how its vulnerabilities are found instead.
#   3. component added    — a COMPONENT name that is not in the Buildroot package list is
#                          ADDED to the inventory. That is how the kernel, U-Boot and the
#                          Rockchip SDK get checked at all: they are in the image but are
# MODE: gate (default — findings can block a release) or report-only (counted and listed,
#       never blocking; for components whose fix is a version rebase, not per-CVE triage).
# A wrong CPE is worse than a missing one: it reports a component as clean instead of
# reporting it as unchecked. Verify against the NVD CPE dictionary before adding a row
# Coverage-gap closure 2026-08-12: the 19 components the report listed as NOT
# CHECKED. Every name below was resolved against the NVD CPE dictionary on
# 2026-08-12 (keyword search incl. upstream aliases: cdialog, v4l-utils, GNU
# libiconv, GNU time). Exactly one has an NVD identity — GNU nano. The NONE
# rows mean NVD has never issued an advisory under any name for the project;
# their vulnerabilities reach us through upstream releases and distro
# advisories, which the quarterly review of this file is the checkpoint for.

column6: NOTES
First-party daemon — no NVD presence. Found by our own testing and by reports to security@joralllc.com.
First-party console (static HTML/JS + CGI shell scripts) — no NVD presence.
First-party CLI — no NVD presence.
glibc argp() extracted as a standalone library for uclibc; no NVD CPE dictionary entry under argp or argp-standalone. Link-time helper, no network exposure.
No NVD CPE dictionary entry. Interactive bandwidth monitor, operator-invoked only.
Data-only package (Mozilla CA trust store snapshot), ships no executable code; no NVD CPE dictionary entry. Currency of the trust store is a maintenance concern, not a CVE-matching one.
No NVD CPE dictionary entry. Operator diagnostic tools for the CAN bench (candump/cansend); not started by any init script.
No NVD CPE dictionary entry under dialog or its upstream name cdialog (keyword matches are unrelated products). Local TUI helper.
No NVD CPE dictionary entry. Local input-device diagnostic.
No NVD CPE dictionary entry (verified 2026-08-12 — the project has never had an NVD advisory). Local process monitor.
Buildroot-internal shell scripts, not an upstream codebase; no NVD presence possible. Reviewed as part of our own image, not via advisories.
Buildroot-internal init scripts; same as ifupdown-scripts.

Pulled in by swupdate as its sw-description parser. No NVD CPE dictionary entry under either plausible vendor - queried cpe:2.3:a:libconfig:libconfig and cpe:2.3:a:hyperrealm:libconfig (upstream org) on 2026-08-15, both 0 results. Vulnerabilities would surface via swupdate advisories or upstream release notes.
No NVD CPE dictionary entry (DRM CVEs are tracked against the kernel, which is checked separately as linux-kernel). Userspace wrapper library.
No NVD CPE dictionary entry for GNU libiconv (iconv CVEs in NVD are glibc's implementation, which this uclibc image does not ship).
Buildroot declares no CPE_ID for this package; vendor/product verified against the NVD CPE dictionary (cpe:2.3:a:netfilter:libnftnl).
Weak-symbol stub library, effectively empty on Linux; no NVD presence.
No NVD CPE dictionary entry under libv4l or v4l-utils. V4L2 CVEs are kernel-side, checked under linux-kernel.

Rockchip RV1106 vendor kernel (sysdrv/source/kernel), not a Buildroot package. Refreshed 5.10.160 -> 5.10.252 on Rockchip develop-5.10, 2026-08-21 (see media/joral/kernel-currency-plan.md); built and packed, bench pass and reflash still owed before shipment. The refresh took the match count from 5155 to 2867 (measured before/after, 2026-08-21) - 2288 records retired by 92 stable releases. The remaining 2867 are overwhelmingly in subsystems and drivers this SoC configuration does not build. Remediation is the re-base cadence itself, not 2867 individual dispositions - 5.10 stable EOL is Dec 2026, so a further move is already scheduled on a trigger; see the OpenSSL/kernel currency item in media/joral/cra-compliance-plan.md.
Verified in the NVD CPE dictionary (cpe:2.3:a:gnu:nano, 178 versioned entries).

Closed-source Rockchip media/ISP/NPU libraries shipped as binaries (librkaiq, rockit, librknnmrt). No NVD CPE exists for them, so nothing can be queried; vulnerabilities in them reach us only through Rockchip release notes or our own testing. Recorded here so the gap is on the record rather than absent from the inventory.
Buildroot-internal rootfs skeleton (directory layout and stock config files); not an upstream codebase.
Buildroot-internal rootfs skeleton for sysv init; same as skeleton-init-common.

The in-product update mechanism itself (Annex I #7), added to the image 2026-08-14. Buildroot declares no CPE_ID for it. Verified against the NVD CPE dictionary 2026-08-15: cpe:2.3:a:swupdate:swupdate is the sbabic/swupdate project (dictionary titles 'SWUpdate 2024.12', 'SWUpdate 2026.05'), not a namesake.
GNU time has no NVD CPE dictionary entry (keyword matches are unrelated products). Local measurement tool.

Buildroot-internal wrapper for the external cross-toolchain; ships runtime libs whose upstream (uclibc-ng, gcc libs) has no per-image NVD identity. Toolchain currency is tracked with the vendor-base items.

Rockchip vendor U-Boot (sysdrv/source/uboot), not a Buildroot package. Same remediation model as the kernel — the vendor fork cannot be bumped independently of the SoC support. Reachability matters here: U-Boot is not network-facing in this product (no netboot, no USB mass-storage boot path enabled), so its findings are not release-blocking on their own.
Buildroot-internal seed-preservation script; not an upstream codebase.

Vendored third-party library (media/joral/eipscanner submodule), statically linked into the daemon. No NVD CPE dictionary entry exists for it, so it cannot be queried; monitored by watching the upstream repository. It parses EtherNet/IP from the network, so it is the highest-value target in this list for our own fuzzing under Annex I Part II periodic testing.
First-party daemon — no NVD presence by definition. Vulnerabilities are found by our own testing (make test, hardware bench TC-S* cases) and by reports to security@joralllc.com per SECURITY.md.
Rockchip closed-source NPU runtime — no CPE. Optional at build time (-DHAVE_RKNN); the float reference path runs without it.
Vendored vendor header, no code shipped from it beyond what the daemon compiles against. No CPE.
First-party React SPA + CGI shell scripts. Same as above. Note that its npm build-time dependency tree is NOT covered by this gate and is not shipped in the image (only the built bundle is).
